name: gcal-event-updated-to-meeting-note

revival.why: The 2026-10-20 retirement assumed a Notion Meetings database moves a note when its linked calendar event is rescheduled. It does not. Found on the Neha Hebbar note (event m9hfa9ru0a3gv89nsptu9ltrco): moved 11 Nov 09:30 -> 12 Nov 10:00 SGT, note still on the old time hours later.

previous_retirement.reason: The Meeting Notes data source was converted to a Notion Meetings database (Full Page Meeting Notes, early access). In a Meetings database the linked calendar event supplies the note's title, date and Notion-member attendees, and Notion updates them when the event changes, so this Zap's job is now native.
previous_retirement.classic_handoff_disabled: 2026-10-20 — the classic hand-off Zap "Updated Meeting -> hand off to durable" was turned off in the Zapier UI.
previous_retirement.how_to_revive: `enable-workflow 019fb770-139b-74ca-bf9b-fec7ea0c9c3b` and turn the classic hand-off Zap back on. No republish needed; the version is intact.

revival.table_still_populated: Checked 2026-11-11: [Table] Meeting Note IDs still gets a row per new note, keyed on the occurrence id (e.g. m9hfa9ru0a3gv89nsptu9ltrco, 7gqqej0vk0bsqq970rg12sjq98), so the lookup works unchanged.
revival.post_merge: Done 2026-11-11: published as 01a1cb26-9b66-7670-b399-851e0262a428 (run 43045073403), then enable-workflow at 15:08Z; get-workflow reports the event_updated trigger active. The classic hand-off Zap stays off.

trigger.authentication_note: work.flowers Google Calendar connection (Google Calendar dennis@work.flowers), the same one workflowers-events-to-scw-busy polls.
trigger.trigger_note: Native polling trigger again since 2026-11-11 (it was a catch hook fed by a classic hand-off Zap from 2026-10-15). Zapier fixed W6ZE93-VMEWP (verified 2026-10-28), so an event already delivered re-fires on each new `updated`, which is exactly a reschedule. The raw Google event path in normalizeInput is the one this trigger feeds. Fires ~60 times a day; everything but a real reschedule of a meeting with a note exits at a free step.
trigger.params_note: expand_recurring: false, as before the hand-off and as on the sibling calendar Zaps. A single-occurrence edit arrives keyed by occurrence id; a whole-series edit arrives as the master and skips.

tables.01JZCVG73MBWWB0357CEPS4903: [Table] Meeting Note IDs — read for the page lookup, written back to keep Start/End/iCal UID current. Owned by the meeting-note-db-updates Notion Worker.

replaces_classic_zap: Updated Meeting -> Update Meeting Note in Notion
description: Google Calendar event updated on dennis@work.flowers -> if it is a reschedule of a meeting with a Notion note, update the note Date and the date in its title. Looks the page up in [Table] Meeting Note IDs on the per-occurrence Google event id; update-only, never creates.

handoff.why: Durables dedupe trigger deliveries on the raw record id (Zapier bug W6ZE93-VMEWP, confirmed 2026-09-08). The native event_updated trigger sends the bare Google occurrence id, so it fired only on first sighting (300 runs, 300 distinct ids, 2026-09-07 → 2026-10-14) and a reschedule never reached this update-only Zap. A classic Zap (which dedupes on id + updated) forwards real reschedules here.
handoff.classic_zap: Updated Meeting → hand off to durable
handoff.classic_trigger: Google Calendar New or Updated Event · calendar dennis@work.flowers · Expand Recurring Events: No · connection 02a752ba-ba43-86d2-b9f7-dc031d6d1aa5
handoff.classic_prefilter: Zapier Tables Find Record ([Table] Meeting Note IDs, Event ID = occurrence id) + Filter (found, not cancelled, timed, start or end differs). Both free, so only real reschedules of events that have a meeting note cost the 1-task POST — the raw trigger fires ~60 times a day.

payload.id: <event id>_<updated> (dedupe key, MUST change per edit: the catch hook also drops a repeated top-level id)

handoff.classic_zap_enabled: 2026-10-15 — confirmed by Dennis. Not machine-verifiable: classic Zaps are exposed by neither the SDK CLI nor MCP.

The classic Zap "Updated Meeting -> hand off to durable" stays OFF; its catch URL https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/20495893/omxtpUyRac5QSs8W/ stops being this Zap trigger on the republish.
